name: Chrome Diopside
physical: Traditionally linked to comfort around the heart area
Associated with a lively, refreshed feeling
Kept nearby by many for relaxation and calm
summary: Chrome diopside is a vivid forest-green gem colored by chromium, used by crystal lovers to open the heart and nurture love, renewal and compassion.
intro: Chrome diopside is a deep, vivid green that sits somewhere between emerald and fresh pine. The color comes from small amounts of chromium in the diopside, a calcium magnesium silicate, and it can be strikingly rich in stones from Siberia. Faceted gems are usually small, since large clean crystals are rare, but they are bright, crisp and affordable compared with emerald. Rough specimens appear as glassy green crystals in dark rock. Because it can look so much like emerald at a fraction of the price, it earned the nickname Siberian emerald, though the stone itself is softer and has distinct cleavage that requires careful setting.
history: Diopside was named in 1800 by the French mineralogist Rene Just Hauy from the Greek words for double and appearance, referring to the two different ways the prism faces seem to look when the crystal is viewed along its length. The gem-grade chrome variety was first found in Yakutia, in Russian Siberia, in the 1990s, near the Inagli massif, though the best material has since been found in other places. It is a relatively recent entry in jewelry, and there is no old folklore attached to it. The modern lore draws on the heart and nature associations of green stones in general.
meaning: Chrome diopside is considered a stone of the heart and of fresh growth. Crystal healers link its deep forest green to the heart chakra and describe it as opening the way to compassion, kindness and forgiveness, both for others and for yourself. It is a popular companion when starting over after a loss, a move or a breakup, because its energy is said to be gentle but steadily hopeful. Some people also associate it with abundance in the sense of a rich, full life rather than money alone. Traditionally it is thought to bring a feeling of vitality and refreshment, like a walk in a deep woods, and is kept nearby by those who want to feel calmer and more balanced emotionally.
howToUse: Wear chrome diopside as a pendant or earrings so it rests near the heart, and use it as a touchstone: when you feel guarded or tense, touch the stone and take three slow breaths. Faceted pieces suit jewelry, while raw crystals are good for the center of a heart-chakra layout with rose quartz and green aventurine. Place a small stone in a plant pot or garden for symbolic growth. During meditation, hold it in your hand over the center of your chest and picture a green light spreading outward. Avoid rings, which risk knocks and chipping.
care: Chrome diopside is moderately hard but has cleavage, so avoid hard knocks and ultrasonic cleaners. It can be rinsed in lukewarm water with mild soap and dried with a soft cloth. Cleanse it with moonlight, sound, smoke or by placing it on a bed of clear quartz. Brief sunlight is safe. Store it separately from harder gems such as sapphire or diamond to prevent scratches, and remove it before heavy work or sports to keep the edges from chipping.
identify: Chrome diopside shows a saturated, slightly bluish to yellowish green, with strong clarity but often tiny inclusions. Emerald tends to be softer in tone and has more visible internal fractures called jardin. Green glass and green tourmaline are common substitutes; tourmaline is harder and often more varied in color, while glass shows bubbles. Chrome diopside is typically sold small, so very large perfect stones at low prices are suspect. Most gem material is untreated.

faq.q: What is chrome diopside good for?
faq.a: Chrome diopside is used for heart-centered work such as compassion, forgiveness and emotional renewal. People wear it near the chest as a reminder to stay open, kind and hopeful during change.

faq.q: Is chrome diopside a real gemstone?
faq.a: Yes. It is a genuine gem variety of diopside colored by chromium. It is softer than emerald and has cleavage, so it is best worn in pendants and earrings rather than daily rings.

faq.q: Can chrome diopside go in water?
faq.a: Yes, a quick rinse in lukewarm water with mild soap is safe, and the stone is not water sensitive. Avoid ultrasonic cleaners and sudden temperature changes, and dry it gently with a soft cloth.
